setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Reviewer considers this Dark Star possibly the most tripped-out ever played, and praises the end of Sugar Magnolia; Reviewer hears a feel of Eyes in the Dark Star jam, in a different key, possibly its seed [13][15]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Garcia pushes the tempo down a full step at one noticeable point in this Jack Straw [11]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Reviewer hears one of the slowest, most staccato Casey Jones versions from this era [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-10-31.142426.sbd.gans.eaton.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 136 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: The first few notes of Bertha and Jack Straw are missing, and a reel flip occurs in Tennessee Jed [1]
- **gd1971-10-31.sbd.miller.79011.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 15 songs; 78 min; rated 4.75/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Keith's piano is crisp and present on this first-set transfer, unlike the Dick's Picks Volume 2 release where he is hard to hear; Keith's keyboard sits far too high in the mix during Bertha, among other mix anomalies; Reel flip in Tennessee Jed was repaired with a crossfade; first notes of Bertha and Jack Straw are missing [2][6][12]
- **gd71-10-31.prefm.unknown.16781.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 4 songs; 19 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: This pre-FM broadcast master lacks most of the first set, including Bertha, Loser, El Paso, Jack Straw and Casey Jones [5]

## Around the show

- Sold-out show at the newly renovated Ohio Theatre; the band asked the crowd to jump on the floor, not the seats [8]
- Jerry Garcia opened on steel guitar with the New Riders of the Purple Sage; Pigpen was absent through illness [8]
- Reviewer says this first-set source pairs with Dick's Picks Volume 2 to give both sets of the show [7]
- Reviewer finds the first-set edit has better instrument separation than the Dick's Picks edit of the second set [9]
- Reviewer calls the setlist standard for fall 1971 and finds instrument separation better than on Dick's Picks 2 [10]
- The deliberate, slowed-down pacing of the show differs from the usual 1971 shows, according to the reviewer [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-10-31.142426.sbd.gans.eaton.miller.flac1644**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Master Reel (7in @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) > Dat (Panasonic SV-3700/44.1k) [1]. Also: Transferred from DATs from David Gans and Rob Eaton; the second set is on Dick's Picks 2 [1]
- **gd1971-10-31.sbd.miller.79011.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) D [2]. Also: The reviewer credits Charlie Miller's transfer of this soundboard with doing the recording justice [6]
- **gd71-10-31.prefm.unknown.16781.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
